I'm not trying to knock you or anything, but I don't think video games would be the best thing for dealing with depression. Video games rely on instant gratification, get that kill and a quick hit of dopamine. Eventually you get addicted to this instant gratification and long - term life goals become harder. Hobbies based around delayed gratification, such as learning guitar or working out, are better in the long run because you get that huge Dopamine boost when you do achieve it.

That's not to say that video games are bad or anything, just play them in moderation.

Instant gratification in general is horrible for us, and the worst thing is that we are surrounded by it in the modern world. TL;DR: Vitamin D (like 5000-10,000 IU a day)

I've have dysthymia pretty much my whole life, so depression has been kinda the norm for me. I spent the last 2 years on an SSRI, which seemed to help somewhat. It boosts serotonin levels, and for some reason, boosting serotonin levels helps, though there isn't clear evidence that SSRIs actually help much.

However, recently I've came across this interesting study: vitamin D regulates the synthsis of seratonin. Huh. Just last year I had basic blood workup done (for a standard health checkup), and found my level was really low, like the kind of low you get by being in the hold of boat for 4 months with zero sunlight. Now, I start my day off with 6000 IU of vitamin D, and the depression seems have solved itself. Dropped the anti-depressant, and I didn't fall back into depression. Sometimes I take another 4000 IU halfway through the day, just because it feels good. Hasn't solved all my problems , but I don't feel too depressed to move anymore. Sometimes my brain still tries to make me lay there, depressed, but eventually the Vitamin D kicks in, and I start feeling like doing something else. Many times it actually feels like a high, kind of like the good feeling from being at the beach all day, without actually have to be at the beach all day. Though, perhaps this "high" is simply what a normal human should feel like.

I think the reason vitamin D helps depression is that through serotonin (and likely other means), it enhances stem cell proliferation and differentiation (study). In my head, this seems to mean it basically enhances the neurogenesis of the brain. It should help your brain create new pathways to unstuck itself ... so you don't just sit there unable to feel like doing anything.

Other benefits: better bone health, improved dietary control, better/stronger muscle control, better immune response, reduced allergies, helps with autism, prolly much more. It's absolutely absurd that people don't know about how important vitamin D is. A cynical part of me wonders if the medical industry makes more money selling you tons of drugs to fix all the problems stemming from deficient vitamin D ... it's likely true. I hope they aren't actually suppressing the knowledge, but judging from how profit tends to make corporations do that, I would not be surprised.

I'd recommend everyone (even those without depression) to get their levels checked. Something like 70% of Americans are deficient, and D is an absurdly important vitamin. I believe the deficiency is just as prevalent in many other parts of the world.
